issues.description: Command names use plural form (quickmarks_reload, bookmarks_reload) while every sibling command in the file is singular (quickmark_add, quickmark_save, quickmark_load, bookmark_add, bookmark_load)
issues.detail: Five of six reviewers flag this as a naming-convention break. The command-surface vocabulary speaks two dialects for one concept, breaks LSP-style substitutability across the command-name family, and cannot be derived from a stated rule. Recommended fix: rename to quickmark_reload / bookmark_reload (or change the others). Pike rates it P2 (naming nit) while Knuth, Hickey, Torvalds, Liskov, and Dijkstra rate it P1.

issues.description: reload() is not atomic on parse failure — clears marks before re-reading, leaving the manager silently empty if parsing raises
issues.detail: self.marks.clear() runs first; any exception from _init_lineparser() or _parse_line() (InvalidUrlError, IO error, malformed user edit) leaves marks lost with no rollback and no 'changed' emit. The postcondition should be 'either marks reflects current disk state, or marks is unchanged and an error is raised.' Fix: build a new OrderedDict locally, parse fully, then swap into self.marks atomically before emitting changed.

issues.description: End-to-end .feature scenarios invoke ':bookmarks-reload' / ':quickmarks-reload' (hyphenated) — verify they actually map to the underscore-named Python methods
issues.detail: Knuth and Hickey treat this as a P1 risk that the e2e scenarios may not exercise the new code at all because the names do not match the methods defined. Dijkstra notes the underscore-to-dash mapping is likely correct by qutebrowser convention but the author should have stated it (rates P2). At minimum the mapping must be verified before merge; if it is wrong, the e2e tests are vacuous.

issues.description: reload() changes __init__'s observable contract by emitting 'changed' during construction where the old inline parse did not
issues.detail: Before the refactor, the constructor populated self.marks silently. After, __init__ calls reload() which emits changed once at the end. Any observer attached between construction and _init_savemanager (or future listeners) now sees an extra signal. Either parameterize reload to skip the emit during construction, inline the initial load, or explicitly document that construction emits changed. Torvalds rates P2, Liskov and Dijkstra rate P1.

issues.description: reload() bypasses the existing public clear() method, smuggling a second clear-semantics into the class
issues.detail: The class already has a clear() method that does self.marks.clear() + self.changed.emit(). reload() calls self.marks.clear() directly to suppress the intermediate emit, creating two undocumented ways to empty self.marks with different signal behavior. Either factor out a private _clear_silent() with a documented contract, or call clear() and accept the double-emit with documentation.

issues.description: _init_lineparser() is now called repeatedly across the object lifetime with no stated idempotence/re-entrancy contract
issues.detail: Originally called exactly once at construction; now called once at construction (via reload) and again on every reload(). Whether LineParser is safe to re-instantiate on the same path mid-flight, whether it rebinds vs mutates, and whether the prior parser's resources leak is unstated. Either document idempotence/re-entrancy, or have reload() reuse the existing parser. Liskov and Pike rate P2, Dijkstra rates P1.

issues.description: reload() has no stated precondition/postcondition/frame — contract is UNREASONED for a now-public method
issues.detail: What if the save-manager is writing concurrently? What if a line is malformed mid-file? The previous inline path was equally undisciplined, but factoring it out makes the contract public. Author should state: precondition (file exists or absent, both legal), postcondition (self.marks equals parsed contents at some point during the call; changed emitted exactly once), frame (only self.marks and self._lineparser change).

issues.description: Tests cover only the happy path — failure-mode and edge-case contracts of reload() are unverified
issues.detail: Missing tests for: (a) reload with empty file clears marks, (b) reload after file deletion, (c) reload with malformed line preserves prior state or fails cleanly, (d) reload mid-save, (e) 'changed' fires exactly once, (f) no-op reload behavior. These cases are precisely where the feature must work (the user edited the file and reloaded) and would also drive the atomicity fix. Per Dijkstra: TESTED-NOT-PROVED.

issues.description: End-to-end Gherkin scenarios have empty/missing titles while every other scenario in the file is descriptively titled
issues.detail: Both new scenarios use bare 'Scenario:' headers. Existing scenarios (e.g. 'Saving a quickmark (:quickmark-add)') are titled. A scenario name is the documentation; missing titles make failures less legible and break the file's voice. Suggested: 'Reloading bookmarks (:bookmark-reload)' / 'Reloading quickmarks (:quickmark-reload)'.

issues.description: Two new command methods are near-duplicates differing only in objreg key and message string
issues.detail: quickmarks_reload and bookmarks_reload are structurally identical. The UrlMarkManager supertype already factors the shared behavior at the model layer; the command layer duplicates the call site. Acceptable for two instances; flag for refactor (parameterized helper or shared implementation) if a third urlmark variety is added.

issues.description: Test does not verify the pre-reload state was actually loaded before reload replaces it
issues.detail: test_reload writes one URL, constructs the manager, writes a different URL, calls reload(), and asserts only the post-reload state. It never asserts that the initial example.com mark was present after construction — the test would pass even if __init__ silently did nothing. Add an assertion on bm.marks after construction and before the second write.

issues.description: Test does not pin 'disk is truth, including deletions' semantics
issues.detail: The reload() method calls self.marks.clear() so deletions on disk should be reflected, but the unit test doesn't exercise the case where the new file has fewer entries than memory. Add: write file, construct, write smaller file, reload, assert marks shrank.

issues.description: Test does not exercise save-manager interaction after reload
issues.detail: A subsequent mutate-and-save after reload would verify reloading didn't break the save-manager wiring — covering read → mutate → write end-to-end. One additional line would close the loop.

issues.description: _init_lineparser name implies one-shot init but is now re-run on every reload
issues.detail: The underscore-prefix and _init_ name both signal construction-time setup. Calling it from reload() works only because subclasses happen to be idempotent — contract isn't stated. Rename to _open_lineparser / _load_lineparser, or split construction from reading.

issues.description: No literate/explanatory comment in __init__ about ordering of reload() and _init_savemanager
issues.detail: A one-line comment above self.reload() in __init__ stating that reload() is also the initial-load path, and that _init_savemanager must run after the first reload() so the manager is not asked to save a partially-loaded state, would make the ordering invariant readable without running the code.

issues.description: message.info text is now coupled to the e2e test as part of the command's public contract
issues.detail: reload() emits 'changed' and the command prints 'Quickmarks reloaded.' The e2e test asserts on the exact message string, so drift between the asserted and emitted text will fail the e2e for reasons unrelated to reload behavior. Either factor the string to a single source or accept that the string is part of the API and document that.

issues.description: No documentation update for the new commands
issues.detail: qutebrowser ships generated command documentation. A new top-level command added without a doc/help update is a command whose specification exists only in source. State where the command is documented to end users.

issues.description: GOOD-TASTE note: __init__ refactored to call reload() eliminates duplicate parse logic (positive observation)
issues.detail: The change replaces the in-line parse loop in __init__ with a call to the new reload() method, so the load-from-disk path exists once instead of twice. This is the right shape for the patch and the part that earns the ACCEPT half of the verdict. Hickey and Pike echo this as the correct decomposition.

synthesis.summary: The panel broadly accepts the underlying refactor — extracting the disk-read into a shared reload() on UrlMarkManager and having __init__ delegate to it removes a duplicated parse loop and is the right shape for the feature. The single strongest unified claim is the naming break: five of six reviewers (Knuth, Hickey, Torvalds, Liskov, Dijkstra at P1; Pike at P2) flag that the new commands are plural (quickmarks_reload, bookmarks_reload) while every adjacent command is singular, and four reviewers raise an adjacent risk that the e2e feature file's hyphenated invocations may not actually exercise the new methods. The second unified P1 thread is that reload() is under-specified: it is not atomic on parse failure (clears then re-reads), bypasses the existing public clear() method, silently changes __init__'s 'changed'-signal semantics, and reuses _init_lineparser with no stated idempotence contract; tests cover only the happy path. The strongest preserved disagreement is on the atomicity severity — Knuth, Liskov, and Dijkstra rate the silent-empty-on-failure outcome P1 (with build-then-swap as the fix), while Pike rates the same defect P2 and Hickey/Torvalds do not flag it at all. Recommended gate: rename to singular, verify or correct the hyphen/underscore command mapping, make reload() atomic via build-then-swap, reconcile the dual clear-paths, document __init__'s emit semantics, and add malformed-file / deletion / mid-save tests before merge.
